questions.prompt: How does Bonevac initially frame ethics within philosophy?
choices: A As pure metaphysics with no practical stake.
B As the most practical part of philosophy—focused on how to live and what to do (philosophy as pursuit of good judgment).
C As only logic puzzles about language.
D As identical to empirical psychology.
questions.explain: Ethics is philosophy’s practical side: how to live and what to do.

questions.prompt: Which trio of questions does he call fundamental in ethics?
choices: A What to publish, what to cite, how to footnote.
B What to be, what to do, and how to decide.
C What to price, what to tax, how to vote.
D What to dream, what to forget, how to sleep.
questions.explain: Character, action, and decision method are core.

questions.prompt: Which five practices does Confucius (as cited) treat as constituting perfect virtue?
choices: A Wealth, fame, power, beauty, and luck.
B Seriousness, generosity, sincerity, diligence, and kindness.
C Irony, cynicism, detachment, silence, and solitude.
D Only ritual without character traits.

questions.prompt: In the Phaedrus chariot image, reason is:
choices: A One of the two horses.
B The charioteer driving desire (unruly) and emotion (usually cooperating but needing control).
C Irrelevant to the soul’s motion.
D Identical to appetite.
questions.explain: Reason drives; desire unruly; emotion needs control.

questions.prompt: Aristotle’s Nicomachean Ethics opening claim is that every action/art/inquiry aims at:
choices: A Random preference with no shared aim.
B Some good—the good being that at which all things aim.
C Only political office.
D Purely aesthetic pleasure.
